content.comment_body: I'm running tests with [product_name] Web Editor to build a custom web page for [product_name] [version_no]. It looks like adding my own JavaScript library isn't supported. If I place my custom_library.js in the project's js folder, that file isn't loaded to the [product_name] SD card and my library can't be accessed. Only the default libraries seem to be loaded. Each time I upload my project, old folders are cleared and replaced with default ones, so copying my library directly onto the SD card is lost during each reload. Has anyone found a way to load a custom JavaScript library? Thanks.

Hello, If you download from [product_name] Web Editor, your library isn't included in the project and is removed. I am not aware of a solution for this issue. Your only option is to finish the [product_name] Web Editor work first (so you don't have to download again), and then add your custom files after that. Hope this helps.

That may work, but it's not an ideal workflow. If I make a mistake, I'd have to reload my project, remove the SD card, copy my library, reinsert the SD card, test everything, repeat the steps, and so on. After a few cycles of this, I'd probably just try to sell my [product_name] [version_no] out of frustration. Thanks.

analysis.insight_summary: Users face substantial difficulties integrating custom JavaScript libraries into their projects using [product_name] Web Editor for [product_name] devices. The lack of support for persistent custom files disrupts usual development workflows and causes significant frustration. Suggested workarounds, such as adding files after project completion, are inconvenient and reduce overall satisfaction with the product.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the ability to permanently add and use custom JavaScript libraries in projects created with [product_name] Web Editor, even after project updates or transfers. They want their enhancements to remain intact during reloads and project revisions.
